title: TransactionReconciled
description: The terminal outcome of reconciling one transaction. Until this event existed a transaction's projected status never advanced past RECEIVED, so no match rate or error rate could be computed from the read model — the dashboard omitted both rather than divide by an empty population. The explanation fields are part of the contract, not an afterthought: a downstream consumer that can see the outcome but not the reasoning cannot act on it.

transactionId.description: The transaction this outcome belongs to. Also the Kafka partition key, so outcomes stay ordered against the TransactionReceived that preceded them.

outcome.description: Coarse business outcome. Deliberately narrower than `classification`: a consumer building a dashboard should not have to know all nine engine classifications to answer 'did this settle'.

classification.description: The engine's own classification, carried through unflattened so an analyst sees exactly which case fired.

matchedEntryIds.description: Counterpart entries. A list because 1:N settlement is real — one statement line closing several postings. Empty when nothing matched.

ruleSetVersion.description: The rule set in force, so a decision stays explainable years after the rules change.

candidatePoolSize.description: How many candidates survived blocking. Distinguishes 'the only option' from 'one of forty', which is the difference between a safe auto-match and a lucky one.

reconciledAt.description: When the engine reached this outcome.
